Selecting an inline chip together with the ordinary text right next to it and applying the action
visible in the image doesn't format both parts the same way — one part changes and the other
doesn't, from that single action. Selecting plain text on its own and applying the same action to
it works as expected, so the chip's presence is what causes the split. See the attached screenshots

The fix is in place and verified. Here's a summary of the work.

## The bug

Selecting an inline chip (the `DateTimeNode` "Sat Jun 20 2026" pill) together with adjacent plain text and pressing **Bold** formats only one part — the chip is "left unformatted" while the text changes (or vice-versa). Plain text alone always works.

## Root cause

The chip is a `DecoratorTextNode` (a `DecoratorNode`, **not** a `TextNode`), so it stores its own format and is formatted out-of-band. `FORMAT_TEXT_COMMAND` is handled by **two independent listeners** that both run for one keypress:

1. **`@lexical/rich-text`** (`COMMAND_PRIORITY_EDITOR`) → `RangeSelection.formatText()`. It skips non-text nodes and formats text with **alignment** — the direction is decided by the first text node and everything converges to it.
2. **`DecoratorTextExtension`** (`COMMAND_PRIORITY_LOW`, runs first) → naively called `node.toggleFormat()` on each chip, deciding direction from the chip's *own* current format with **no alignment**.

When the chip and the text start with different bold states, the two handlers move in **opposite directions**, so a single Bold press fails to make both parts consistent. (`packages/lexical/src/LexicalUpdates.ts:917` confirms priorities dispatch 4→0, so the extension runs before rich-text and, returning `false`, both execute.)

## The fix

`packages/lexical-extension/src/DecoratorTextExtension.ts` — the extension now mirrors `formatText`'s alignment: it computes the target format from the first `TextNode` in the selection and aligns every decorator node to it (falling back to the first decorator when the selection has no text, e.g. a pure `NodeSelection` of chips). A single action now formats chip and text the same way.

## Verification

- New test `packages/lexical-extension/src/__tests__/unit/DecoratorTextFormat.test.ts` covers all four initial-format combinations plus the exact screenshot scenario (chip bold + text plain → both bold).
- **Fails on the original code** (the divergent cases) and **passes with the fix**.
- Full `@lexical/extension` unit suite: 61 passed. ESLint clean. TypeScript clean (the only TS errors are pre-existing missing-optional-dep errors in the playground, unrelated to these files).

No public API or serialization format changed, so this is backwards-compatible.
